summary: Condensed chapter/section roadmaps and notation explanations.
Merged repeated CPWL representability narration while retaining distinct max-tree and dimension-only depth proofs.
Shortened monotonicity and convexity induction prose while preserving every base, closure, and output step.
Shortened Shapley proof narration while retaining finite maximum attainment, nonnegative discounts, both saddle inequalities, and the every-subgame conclusion.
Condensed ReLU game proof setup, base case, mirrored case, ties, and forced affine output.
retained_qualifications: First ICNN weight matrix unconstrained; subsequent and output weights nonnegative.
Convex and nondecreasing activation requirements; affine passthrough qualification.
Composition uses each affine polyhedral cell and preserves continuity.
Uniform depth bound credited through Arora to Wang--Sun and counts final affine output.
Nonnegative possibly >1 structural discounts; policy ties may be nonunique.
ReLU game nonzero rows, sign switching, one-time terminal payoff, affine output, stop-at-zero convention.
Negative-state entropy sign and distinct theta/tau temperatures.

preexisting_ambiguities_not_changed.issue: Domain d^(l) suggests layers after l; text calls f^(L) affine output map rather than identity. The compression preserves the existing formulas and convention.
Finite action sets are not explicitly required to be nonempty, though maxima and policies need that assumption.
Output state has one action but ownership outside displayed S_q partition is unspecified; absorbing cemetery must be understood terminal for the acyclic argument.
Discount times a sign-edge transition is W^(q xor r), equal to absolute W only for the matching sign edge; current text says exactly absolute weight without this qualification.

independent_review.verdict: No new loss of hypotheses, proof steps, or substantive content in changed text. All key mathematical dependencies and roadmap references retained. Existing ambiguities left unchanged.

review_resolution.request: Restore the respective mapping between the two structured classes and their properties.
